The FDA urged citizens to report instances of illegal drug manufacturing or sales, as well as suspected substandard drugs, medical devices and cosmetics, to its commissioner’s office or the nearest district office

The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) seized drugs and cosmetics worth ₹34.51 lakh, cancelled 122 licences and suspended 422 others following enforcement action across the State in October 2026, according to a press note issued by the department on Thursday (November 5, 2026).

The FDA conducted 1,986 inspections of drug manufacturing, sales and other regulated establishments during the month and issued 674 notices. Of these, 1,694 inspections were conducted at drug sales establishments and 292 at manufacturing and other regulated establishments. The department cancelled 105 licences and suspended 367 licences of sales establishments, while 17 licences were cancelled and 55 suspended in the manufacturing and other categories.

The department also carried out 11 search and seizure operations involving alleged violations related to the manufacture, storage and sale of drugs and cosmetics. Two FIRs were registered, and four persons were arrested under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act in connection with the illegal sale of narcotic drugs.

Among the major seizures, FDA officials recovered allopathic drugs worth ₹22.03 lakh from the premises of Phoenix Medicorp in Nagpur on October 7. According to the department, the establishment had stored drugs at unlicensed premises despite surrendering its licences.

In Mumbai, FDA officials seized spurious drugs identified as Empirime tablets and Cardiurex 2 ml, worth ₹1.01 lakh, from INHS Asvini in Colaba on October 29, according to the department.

In separate operations in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar on October 14 and 25, officials seized 199 Nitrosun 10 tablets containing Nitrazepam. Four persons were arrested in connection with their alleged illegal sale.

The FDA also seized cosmetic soaps worth ₹4.05 lakh from Vedas Herbals Mahila Gruh Udyog in Baramati, Pune district, on October 14, for alleged manufacturing without a licence. In Vasai East, officials seized raw materials, packaging materials and machinery worth ₹1.83 lakh from G.B. Cosmetics on October 10 in connection with alleged unlicensed manufacture and sale of nail polish.

The Konkan division recorded the highest number of inspections in October at 556, followed by Pune with 375 and Greater Mumbai with 322. Konkan also accounted for the highest number of regulatory actions at 156, followed by Greater Mumbai with 105 and Pune with 77.

Between April 1 and October 31, the FDA conducted 7,950 inspections across Maharashtra, issued 2,888 notices, cancelled 555 licences and suspended 2,074 licences. The department recorded 2,629 regulatory actions, comprising licence cancellations and suspensions, during the seven-month period.

The FDA urged citizens to report instances of illegal drug manufacturing or sales, as well as suspected substandard drugs, medical devices and cosmetics, to its commissioner’s office or the nearest district office.

articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Critics accused Donald Trump of ignoring voter concerns over the Iran war and affordability ahead of midterm elections and obsessing instead on multiple construction and renovation projects in the capital

U.S. President Donald Trump signed an order on Thursday (November 5, 2026) designating the Oval Office as a national monument, redoubling his focus on beautifying the White House despite a brutal midterms defeat for his Republican Party.

Critics accused Mr. Trump of ignoring voter concerns over the Iran war and affordability ahead of Tuesday’s (November 4, 2026) midterm elections and obsessing instead on multiple construction and renovation projects in the capital.
The day after Democrats won the House of Representatives and Senate, Mr. Trump virtually ignored the result and showed off construction work on his new White House ballroom instead.
This time Mr. Trump’s focus was on the Oval Office, which he has bedecked with gold ornaments since returning to power last year, and the neighboring Cabinet Room.
He said the proclamation would “make it impossible for anybody ever to destroy this incredible space” and prevent future presidents from carrying out any building work on the two rooms.

Mr. Trump’s signing of the order in the Oval Office was not broadcast on major U.S. networks, as he has banned CNN from the rotating “pool” of television outlets that cover White House events.
Mr. Trump did give one nod to the midterms, with a red baseball cap with the word “veto” on the Resolute Desk in front of him.

articles.title: Eisenkot tipped to seek Israel government with backing of Arab lists
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Isaac Herzog held a second day of consultations with political parties on November 5 after the October 27 election; he said he will announce on November 8 whom he will task with trying to form a new government

Israeli President Isaac Herzog said he will announce on Sunday (November 8, 2026) whom he will task with trying to form a new government, after the opposition’s Gadi Eisenkot secured a commanding number of recommendations to replace Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Mr. Herzog held a second day of consultations with political parties on Thursday (November 5, 2026) after the October 27 election, in which neither Mr. Netanyahu — a polarising right-winger who has led Israel through three years of war — nor Mr. Eisenkot — a former military chief promising to restore national unity — secured enough votes for a majority.

Mr. Herzog will make his choice, but traditionally the mandate is given to the person recommended by more parliament members. Sixty-seven picked Mr. Eisenkot, 46 opted for Mr. Netanyahu, while seven abstained.

“The results of the consultations may appear clear, but the authority vested in me by law is to determine who has the ability to form a government, and that is not entirely clear, given the mutual vetoes between the blocs and within the blocs themselves,” Mr. Herzog said on Thursday (November 5, 2026).
“I will try to determine this directly and quickly, in personal talks with some of the party leaders.”

Mr. Eisenkot’s Yashar party said on Thursday (November 5, 2026) that “the citizens of Israel have chosen change and expressed a complete lack of confidence in outgoing Prime Minister Netanyahu and his government”, and called for the “immediate establishment of a national emergency government that will begin working for all citizens of Israel”.
Two Arab-majority lists won an unprecedented 19 seats in the election, making them potential kingmakers if Mr. Eisenkot’s opposition chooses to work with them, which remains unclear.
Both Arab lists on Thursday (November 5, 2026) said they were backing Mr. Eisenkot.
However, another party in Mr. Eisenkot’s camp, right-wing Israel Beiteinu, has repeatedly indicated it will not sit in a government that relies on support from Arab parties.

Party leader Avigdor Liberman, a former Netanyahu ally turned critic, cited as a reason the refusal by Arab parties to explicitly define Hamas as a “terror group” — even though they have repeatedly condemned the organisation’s attack on Israel on October 7, 2023.

articles.title: Foreign Secretary Misri sets stage for Nepal PM’s upcoming India visit
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The Nepali leaders expressed “gratitude for India’s swift and substantial humanitarian and technical assistance in the aftermath of the Bhotekoshi floods”, a joint press release stated

Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri on Thursday (November 5, 2026) met Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah in Kathmandu, with discussions focused on “possible outcomes and initiatives” from the expected upcoming visit of the Himalayan nation’s leader to New Delhi.
Concluding his official engagements in Nepal that spanned Wednesday and Thursday, Mr. Misri also met Nepal Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle and Foreign Minister Sisir Khanal.

“The Foreign Secretary of India highlighted the wide-ranging engagement and overall progress in diverse areas of bilateral cooperation, and discussed possible outcomes and initiatives in the context of the upcoming visit of the Prime Minister of Nepal to India,” stated a joint press release issued by the Ministry of External Affairs and Kathmandu’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
Mr. Misri held detailed talks with his host, Nepali Foreign Secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai, on the “mutually beneficial partnership” between India and Nepal.

Mr. Shah had earlier this year highlighted the border dispute with India in the Lipulekh-Kalapai-Limpiyadhura area that is part of India’s Uttarakhand but claimed by Nepal as a sticking point in ties.
Mr. Shah had sought to involve other countries, such as the United Kingdom and China, in talks on the issue. But India wants the matter to be resolved bilaterally.
The Nepali leaders expressed “gratitude for India’s swift and substantial humanitarian and technical assistance in the aftermath of the Bhotekoshi floods”, the joint press release stated.

Mr. Misri’s discussions with Nepali stakeholders included a “commerce and development partnership, hydropower, physical connectivity, border management, energy and people-to-people ties”, as well as new areas like digital connectivity and AI.
Mr. Misri also met Minister for Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation Biraj Bhakta Shrestha and Minister for Infrastructure Development Sunil Lamsal.
Mr. Shah was sworn in as Prime Minister in March this year following the Gen-Z uprising in Nepal in September 2025 that led to the ouster of the previous government.

articles.title: The ecological fallout of Israel’s war in Gaza
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The destruction of Gaza’s ecosystems underscores the need for accountability under international law

On November 5, 2001, the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) designated November 6 each year as the International Day for Preventing the Exploitation of the Environment in War and Armed Conflict . This recognition underscores the far-reaching impacts of environmental damage caused by armed conflict, including degradation of ecosystems and resource depletion well after the conflict period. This impact often extends beyond the limits of national territories and affects future generations.

Considering the importance of the issue, the International Law Commission (ILC), in its report titled ‘Protection of the Environment in Relation to Armed Conflicts’ (PERAC), adopted 27 draft principles in 2022, which were formally noted by the UNGA on December 7, 2022. The overarching purpose of these principles is to enhance the protection of the environment in relation to armed conflicts. The first principle of the PERAC provides that the principles apply to the protection of the environment before, during and after an armed conflict, including in situations of occupation. In this context, Israel’s responsibility for internationally wrongful acts causing environmental harm arises not only from its ongoing genocide in Gaza but also from its continuing role as an occupying power.

The destruction of Gaza’s ecosystems underscores the need for accountability under international law

On November 5, 2001, the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) designated November 6 each year as the International Day for Preventing the Exploitation of the Environment in War and Armed Conflict . This recognition underscores the far-reaching impacts of environmental damage caused by armed conflict, including degradation of ecosystems and resource depletion well after the conflict period. This impact often extends beyond the limits of national territories and affects future generations.

Considering the importance of the issue, the International Law Commission (ILC), in its report titled ‘Protection of the Environment in Relation to Armed Conflicts’ (PERAC), adopted 27 draft principles in 2022, which were formally noted by the UNGA on December 7, 2022. The overarching purpose of these principles is to enhance the protection of the environment in relation to armed conflicts. The first principle of the PERAC provides that the principles apply to the protection of the environment before, during and after an armed conflict, including in situations of occupation. In this context, Israel’s responsibility for internationally wrongful acts causing environmental harm arises not only from its ongoing genocide in Gaza but also from its continuing role as an occupying power.

fullParagraphs: Attorney General Todd Blanche announced her resignation in a social media post, saying Assistant Attorney General Dhillon had "led the Civil Rights Division with conviction

Indian-American Harmeet Kaur Dhillon has resigned as the U.S. Assistant Attorney General and head of the Justice Department's Civil Rights Division, becoming the first senior official to leave the Trump administration since the mid-term elections.
Attorney General Todd Blanche announced her resignation in a social media post, saying Assistant Attorney General Dhillon had "led the Civil Rights Division with conviction".
“She has defended the civil liberties of every American and enforced the law without fear or favour,” Blanche wrote on X on Thursday (November 5, 2026).
“The department is grateful for her dedicated public service, and we wish her every success in her future endeavours,” he added.

Assistant Attorney General Dhillon, whose law firm was part of Donald Trump’s campaign legal team, told Fox News she resigned of her own volition and withheld her announcement at the request of Susie Wiles, the White House chief of staff, until after Election Day.

“Serving my country as AAG for Civil Rights has been the honour of a lifetime. We ushered in the downfall of illegal DEI, we fought to protect women and girls’ sports, and so much more. I want to thank President Trump for giving me this opportunity. I look forward to what’s next,” Assistant Attorney General Dhillon said in a post on X.
Born in Chandigarh into a Punjabi Sikh family, Dhillon's parents initially moved to London before eventually settling in the United States.

A staunch ally of President Donald Trump, Dhillon ran her own law firm in San Francisco for several years before joining the Justice Department. She is a frequent guest on conservative podcasts and maintains a very active presence on social media.
Unlike her predecessors, she frequently took to social media to post videos about the work her division was undertaking.
She acknowledged in media interviews that she often generated ideas for civil rights investigations based on various posts she encountered on social media.

articles.title: Supreme Court seeks response from NewsClick, Purkayastha on ED plea against High Court order
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: At the outset, the counsel appearing for the ED submitted that they needed four weeks' time as Additional Solicitor General S.V. Raju, representing the agency, was not available

The Supreme Court on Friday (November 6, 2026) sought responses from news portal NewsClick a nd its editor-in-chief Prabir Purkayastha on a plea by the Enforcement Directorate challenging the Delhi High Court order quashing a money laundering case registered for alleged violation of FDI rules.
A Bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana issued notice to NewsClick and Purkayastha and sought their responses in four weeks.
At the outset, the counsel appearing for the ED submitted that they needed four weeks' time as Additional Solicitor General S.V. Raju, representing the agency, was not available.
Justice Bagchi said that the appeal does not inspire confidence.
The counsel for ED further submitted that the Delhi Police was also in the process of challenging the quashing of the FIR related to the predicate offence and sought four weeks' adjournment.

In its plea before the top court, the agency contended that the High Court quashed its enforcement case information report (ECIR) without examining the PMLA case, and there was an inordinate delay of five months in the pronouncement of the judgment.

On May 29, the Delhi High Court had said the continuation of an FIR registered by the Delhi Police's Economic Offences Wing (EOW) was "nothing but a gross abuse of the process of law", and once the FIR under the predicate offence was quashed, the ED's ECIR in the matter was also liable to be closed.

The EOW's 2020 FIR alleged that PPK Newsclick Studio Pvt. Ltd., NewsClick's parent company, received foreign direct investment (FDI) of ₹9.59 crore from Worldwide Media Holdings LLC USA in the financial year 2018-19, in violation of the foreign investment law, which caused a loss to the government exchequer.

articles.title: Keralam Excise Commissioner Seeram Sambasiva Rao shifted amid differences with Minister over bar licence
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Move comes a few days after Excise Minister M. Liju publicly indicated his disapproval on granting of bar licence to a lounge at Kochi airport despite government's objection to a similar application

Keralam Excise Commissioner Seeram Sambasiva Rao has been shifted from the post a few days after Excise Minister M. Liju publicly indicated his disapproval on the granting of bar licence to a lounge at the Kochi airport despite the government's objection to a similar application.
The Additional Excise Commissioner has been given charge in his place. Mr. Rao was appointed to the post in June 2026.

Mr. Liju had said that the department granted two licences without the government’s knowledge. Although application for a third was forwarded to the government, it was communicated that a decision could be taken only after the new Excise policy was adopted by the end of November. Still, proceedings were initiated on a fresh application.

The Minister had said that the Excise Commissioner should have consulted the government before taking the decision. Hinting at a relook at the process of granting bar licences, Mr. Liju had said on Monday that the government would investigate whether bar licences were granted in haste by some officials using loopholes in the system.

He said the previous Left Democratic Front (LDF) government had in 2017 issued an order which enabled Deputy Commissioners to approve applications for upgrading beer and wine parlours to bar licences provided the establishments attain star classification.
Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan had also said on Wednesday that no bar licence would be issued without the government's knowledge.

articles.title: SC issues notice to all office bearers of Keralam unit of Congress over post targeting CJI Surya Kant
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: A post against the CJI from the official X account of the Keralam unit of Congress went viral on October 12, drawing sharp criticism on social media, before it was deleted

Observing that independence of the judiciary is not a matter of "political convenience", the Supreme Court on Friday (November 6, 2026) issued a contempt notice to all office bearers of Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee over a social media post targeting Chief Justice of India Surya Kant.
A bench of justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M. Pancholi said that the Constitution is supreme and no individual or political organisation stands above it.

"Judgments are always open to criticism. Freedom of expression can't be a shield of intimidation to interfere with the administration of justice. Howsoever high position a person occupies, any attempt to undermine the authority of the court needs to be dealt with an iron hand.”
"Authority of the court doesn't require political endorsement; it rests on the rule of law. Where administration of justice is established, the law must take its course," the bench said.
Independence of judiciary is not a matter of political convenience, the court added.

The top court said it has appointed a senior advocate as amicus curiae in the matter to examine whether criminal or civil contempt apply in the matter and also sought Attorney General R. Venkataramani's assistance in the matter.

articles.title: Supreme Court stands firm by March 11 judgment on assessing OBC creamy layer policy
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: As far as the operation of the 2025 batch was concerned, the Court said the service allocation would be in compliance with the March 2026 judgment

The Supreme Court on Friday (November 6, 2026) stood firm by its March 11, 2026 judgment , which upheld the assessment of the OBC non-creamy layer status as per a 1993 Office Memorandum, which excluded parental salary income and agricultural income from the income/wealth test.

A Bench of Justices P.S. Narasimha and R. Mahadevan did not agree with the government’s plea for a “reasonable time” of two years to undertake the necessary exercise of establishing equivalence of posts after consulting stakeholders and formulating an appropriate and uniform policy/mechanism for determination of OBC creamy layer status.

The court clarified that although the result of the Civil Service Examination 2025 was declared on March 6, 2026, the services had still not been allocated to the successful candidates. It said that since the process of allocation was pending, there would be no reasonable justification to defer the implementation of the March 11 judgment. It said the creamy layer principle, as interpreted in the judgment, would govern the allocation of services of OBC candidates selected through the Civil Service Examination 2025.

The judgment on Friday (November 6, 2026) highlighted the Department of Personnel and Training’s (DoPT) assurance, recorded in the March 2026 verdict, that it would create supernumerary posts to accommodate candidates, who are parties in the case and satisfy the non-creamy layer criteria, subject to their fulfilling all the eligibility conditions. The DoPT position had also been recorded in the 21st Report of the Parliamentary Committee on the Welfare of Other Backward Classes.

Justice Mahadevan said the government may accordingly accommodate the candidates, who are parties before the apex court, provided they fulfil the requisite eligibility criteria. The court clarified that the judgment was applicable to the parties before it and would not be used to reopen appointments concluded prior to the verdict.

The government, in its application filed through Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati for a modification of the March 11 judgment, had said a retrospective implementation of the Supreme Court verdict would have significant consequences for recruitment, service allocation, cadre allocation, seniority, admissions and the administration of OBC reservation generally, affecting lakhs.

The court reiterated that individual claims pending before any court, tribunal, or other competent forum or authority should be considered on their own merits. The court expressed no opinion on the merits of such claims. The court extended the timeline for deciding these claims by eight weeks. On March 11, the court had given a six-month deadline.

The court said the Centre was at liberty to formulate its policy concerning reservation and the creamy layer criteria in accordance with the Constitution. It refused to prescribe any timeline for establishing equivalence between posts or consulting stakeholders in the formulation of the creamy layer policy, noting that these issues fell within the domain of the Executive and the Legislature.
Advocate Shashank Ratnoo, who appeared for the candidates, said the Supreme Court’s intervention has put an end to a decade-long injustice.

Senior advocate P. Wilson, who also represents the candidates, said the Centre had been merely trying to delay, even undo a final judgment of the apex court. He criticised that the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) had failed to comply with court directions, Parliamentary Committee recommendations, and its own 1993 rules.

fullParagraphs: The Civil Services exam is conducted annually in three stages - preliminary, main, and interview - to select candidates for the Indian Administrative Services (IAS), Indian Foreign Service (IFS), and Indian Police Service (IPS) and other services.

The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) has declared the results of the Civil Services (Main) Examination 2026, on November 5, 2026, with successful candidates qualifying for the personality test of the highly coveted examination.

The civil services exam is conducted annually in three stages — preliminary, main, and interview — to select candidates for the Indian Administrative Services (IAS), Indian Foreign Service (IFS), and Indian Police Service (IPS) and other services.
Long UPSC prep cycles take heavy toll on aspirants’ mental health
Candidates can follow these steps to check their UPSC results

A candidate who clears the written examination (Main) will proceed to the personality test, also referred to as the UPSC interview. The interview carries 275 marks, while the written Mains examination carries 1,750 marks. The final merit list is prepared using the combined scores of both the main and interview stages of the UPSC examination.
Candidates who qualify for the Mains examination will receive e-summon letters of personality tests (Interviews), which can be downloaded from the commission’s website.
Candidates who may not be able to download their e-Summon letters, should immediately contact the office of the Commission through letter or through the following means
No paper/physical summon letters will be issued for the personality tests (interviews) by the commission.

Dates of personality tests (interviews) of the candidates will be notified in due course, as per the official communication. The interviews will be held at the Office of the Union Public Service Commission at Dholpur House, Shahjahan Road, New Delhi.

Democrats seized control of U.S. Congress after the midterm election on Tuesday (November 3, 2026), winning the Senate and House in a nationwide rebuke of President Donald Trump, likely limiting the rest of his term.

In a massive blue wave across the country, Trump’s Republican Party faced stunning defeats in its strongholds Texas, Georgia, Iowa and Ohio, where it lost the Governor’s posts to the Democrats. The Grand Old Party (GOP) also faced a drubbing in Senate races in Texas, Maine, South Carolina, North Carolina, Kansas, Iowa and Ohio, where Trump campaigned with a simple message, urging voters to pretend that he was on the ballot.

In a historic turn of events in U.S. political history, Texas Democrat James Talarico, a former teacher who ran on a “politics of love”, defeated Attorney General Ken Paxton to win a Senate seat—the first Democrat statewide winner since 1994. Separately, Democrat Gina Hinojosa defeated Republican Governor Greg Abbott, ending decades of Republican rule. Abdul El-Sayed defeated former Republican lawmaker Mike Rogers in Michigan to become the first Muslim elected to the upper chamber of Congress.

articles.title: Key federal panel approves Trump’s arch while it is being challenged in court
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The National Capital Planning Commission voted 8-4 to approve the 76-metre memorial arch near Washington, as three lawsuits challenge it and a judge is expected to rule soon on whether to block construction.
A federal judge late on Thursday (November 5, 2026) blocked the Trump administration from breaking ground on a towering memorial arch for 14 days.

The temporary restraining order by U.S. District Judge Tanya Chutkan, halting the work, represents a major setback for one of President Donald Trump’s most prominent projects in his vision to remake Washington.

The decision followed a series of steps taken earlier on Thursday by the government, including the final approval of the arch by the National Capital Planning Commission in an 8-4 vote after a hearing of nine and a half hours, where dozens of witnesses opposed the construction.

The administration said the work could begin as soon as the approval was in place, the Interior Department issued a final decision authorising construction and the National Park Service published the proper notification.
In issuing the temporary stop, Judge Chutkan said Virginia and the District of Columbia had shown that the immediacy of the construction would cause real harm to the plaintiffs.

“The harm is certain,” she wrote. “Defendants initially notified the court that construction could begin as early as November 5, 2026, if the NCPC approves the project at its meeting that day and the Department of the Interior authorizes construction.” In their filing, Virginia and the District of Columbia warned of traffic pattern distortions, as well as concerns about the impact on mutual aid emergency calls if the arch were to proceed.

“Second, the District and Virginia will incur significant unrecoverable costs. As soon as construction begins, DDOT [District Department of Transportation] will need to expend staff time and operating resources to affirmatively and proactively manage temporary detours, crashes or disabled vehicles,” Judge Chutkan wrote.

The judge’s decision came just over an hour after the commission’s hearing ended. The final vote came after nine and a half hours and scores of people opposing it. The vote broke along federal and local lines. Those in favour work for the administration or are connected to the President, who was pushing for the immediate construction. Opponents represented the city of Washington.
The panel’s Trump-appointed chairman launched the meeting with a gushing appraisal of the towering monument and lauded Mr. Trump for wanting to build it.

“President Trump understands as president and a superb builder that it’s important to our national identity to display who we are through grand monuments,” said Mark Paoletta, the commission’s chairman.

articles.title: Mahabharata, Arthashastra, Rajatarangini manuscripts added to UNESCO memory regional register
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Union Culture Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat hailed the inscriptions as a landmark recognition of India’s extraordinary documentary and civilisational heritage

Manuscripts of the epic Mahabharata, Kalhana’s 12th-century historical chronicle Rajatarangini, and Kautilya’s Arthashastra, a work on governance and statecraft, have been inscribed on UNESCO’s Memory of the World Asia-Pacific Regional Register, officials said on Thursday (November 5, 2026).
PIB Culture made the announcement on X and shared photos of UNESCO certificates.

“A moment of immense pride for India! The Rajatarangini, Mahabharata and Arthashastra have been inscribed in @UNESCO’s Memory of the World Asia-Pacific Regional Register, marking a historic milestone in the global recognition of India’s rich civilisational heritage!” it said.

🇮🇳 A moment of immense pride for India! The Rājataraṅgiṇī, Mahābhārata and Arthaśāstra have been inscribed in @UNESCO's Memory of the World Asia-Pacific Regional Register, marking a historic milestone in the global recognition of India's rich civilisational heritage! https://t.co/LjJwIILhmf
The decision was taken at the 11th Session of the Memory of the World Asia-Pacific Regional Register held in Jakarta, Indonesia, the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA) said.
According to an official, the IGNCA played an important role in preparing the nomination dossiers for all three works.
Union Culture Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat hailed the inscriptions as a landmark recognition of India’s extraordinary documentary and civilisational heritage.

“A moment of immense pride for India! The inclusion of Rajatarangini, Mahabharata and Arthashastra in @UNESCO Memory of the World Asia-Pacific Regional Register is a landmark recognition of India’s extraordinary documentary and civilisational heritage,” he posted.

“These timeless works embody our rich traditions of historical inquiry, philosophical thought and statecraft, whose wisdom continues to inspire humanity. Under the visionary leadership of Hon’ble PM Shri @narendramodi Ji, India’s civilisational legacy is receiving unprecedented global recognition and its rightful place on the world stage,” the minister added.

With the recognition, India’s historical, literary, philosophical and political thought receives wider international acknowledgement, taking the country’s total number of inscriptions in the Regional Register to six, officials said.

articles.title: Indian NGO REACH receives Kochon Prize 2026
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Presented by the Kochon Foundation, an independent Korean non-profit foundation, in partnership with the Stop TB Partnership, the Kochon Prize recognises individuals and organisations that have made significant contributions to the fight against TB

Resource group for Education and Advocacy for Community Health (REACH), a not-for-profit organisation working to strengthen the tuberculosis (TB) response in India, has been awarded the Kochon Prize 2026, becoming the first civil society, non-profit organisation from India to receive this prestigious global recognition for its contributions to combating TB, a press release said.

Presented by the Kochon Foundation, an independent Korean non-profit foundation, in partnership with the Stop TB Partnership, the Kochon Prize recognises individuals and organisations that have made significant contributions to the fight against TB. The 2026 Kochon Prize is shared by REACH, the Centre for Health Solutions, Kenya, and the Marshall Islands TB Control Program. Previous winners from India include L.S. Chauhan (2006), head of the Revised National TB Control Programme, the Indian Council of Medical Research (2017) and Molbio Diagnostics (2024). The award was presented at the Stop TB Partnership Board Meeting held in Indonesia on November 5, 2026.

“Treat the person, not the disease - our journey with TB communities has been just that. We realised early on that overcoming barriers to care means addressing more than clinical needs - it means recognising social, community, family, mental health and situational challenges. That is the essence of integrated care: seeing the whole person, understanding their realities, and doing whatever it takes to ensure that no one is left behind,” said Nalini Krishnan, chairperson and co-founder, REACH.

“REACH is a remarkable and rare organisation that has been consistently ahead of the curve in terms of public health action, and particularly in the field of TB. A women-led organisation, they genuinely care about the people they’re supporting, beyond the numbers, data and reports to donor. However, they combine this with a robust scientific and technical approach and a shrewd understanding of the public health landscape in the country,” said Soumya Swaminathan, chairperson, M. S. Swaminathan Research Foundation and former chief scientist, WHO, who nominated REACH for the award.

“This recognition is testimony to the dedication of the community health workers, TB Nanbans and TB Champions who work alongside us, and to the families affected by TB and non-communicable diseases (NCDs) who have placed their trust in us. We are deeply grateful to their unwavering commitment and fortitude, and are energised to do more to help facilitate equitable access to health,” said Ramya Ananthakrishnan, director, REACH.

articles.title: Documentary highlights role of family physicians in strengthening primary healthcare
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The documentary is intended to initiate wider conversations on reviving primary healthcare networks in urban and rural communities, and recognising neighbourhood doctors as an integral part of the healthcare system

The role of family physicians in ensuring accessible, affordable and patient-centred healthcare came into focus at the premiere of the documentary The Doctor Next Door: A Legacy of Care , screened at the Indian Heritage Academy in Bengaluru earlier this week.

Through accounts of veteran physicians, patients and young medical professionals, the film examines the decline of neighbourhood family practices and the growing fragmentation of healthcare. It highlights how long-standing doctor-patient relationships, built on trust, familiarity and personal attention, remain central to effective primary care.

The documentary draws attention to the rising dependence on specialised and corporate hospital-based treatment, making a case for strengthening family medicine as the foundation of India’s healthcare system.

Swetha Reddy Pitchela, project manager for the documentary, said the film features perspectives from young medical students and practitioners considering careers in general practice, highlighting the need for changes in medical education and healthcare policy to encourage family medicine.

Directed by Ganesh Shankar Raj of Mindia Films and produced in collaboration with the Academy of Family Physicians of India (AFPI), the non-profit documentary explores the enduring relationship between family doctors and patients and the importance of continuity of care in an increasingly specialised healthcare system.

The screening was followed by a panel discussion featuring scientists, medical professionals, senior family physicians and community health advocates. The discussion centred on the challenges facing primary healthcare, the need to strengthen family medicine, and the importance of human relationships in medical practice.
Veteran family physician B.C. Rao was among the contributors to the initiative, alongside representatives of AFPI and other healthcare professionals.

The organisers said the documentary was intended to initiate wider conversations on reviving primary healthcare networks in urban and rural communities and recognising neighbourhood doctors as an integral part of the healthcare system.

articles.title: Amid the sparkle of Deepavali, ophthalmologists sound a note of caution
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Lighting firecrackers is part of the fun of Deepavali. But this should be done safely. Ophthalmologists warn that a moment of carelessness can cause eye injuries ranging from minor abrasions to severe ocular trauma

The sound of firecrackers filling the air is not far away as Deepavali draws closer. But the excitement of bursting firecrackers comes with a word of caution from ophthalmologists as they warn that a moment of carelessness can cause eye injuries ranging from minor abrasions to severe ocular trauma.

M. Elangovan, director, Regional Institute of Ophthalmology and Government Ophthalmic Hospital (RIO-GOH), Chennai, said that there are different types of crackers. “Bursting types (explosive crackers) will produce irregular, small and forcible particles in all directions and are the most dangerous. These particles can travel at such a velocity that they could hit or penetrate any soft surface. Then, there is direct heat injury caused by crackers such as sparklers that can cause scar formations in the cornea or conjunctiva due to the heat generated. Sudden and close exposure to bright light-emitting crackers can also cause bleaching or temporary blackout due to the impact on the rod and cone cells in the retina,” he explained.

Science, Space & Environment Report: Amid the sparkle of Deepavali, ophthalmologists sound a note of caution. This milestone highlights indigenous research, technological self-reliance, and environmental sustainability.

articles.title: Cancer care: Long battle for affordable treatment
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Advances in oncology have improved treatment options, but their benefits remain out of reach for many patients who cannot afford to complete the prescribed course. This is despite the recent decision to cap trade margins on 137 identified non-scheduled anti-cancer medicines, providing some relief, writes Afshan Yasmeen...

A 45-year-old garment factory worker from Bengaluru Rural diagnosed with stage IV-A cancer of the mouth faces an arduous course of treatment: chemotherapy to shrink the tumour, extensive surgery involving reconstruction, followed by radiation and chemotherapy. The cost of medicines and supportive drugs of around ₹93,000 alone, besides treatment costs, are staggering for her family with a modest monthly income of ₹28,000. With funds running out, she is facing the risk of discontinuing the final stages of treatment.

Likewise, a 56-year-old shopkeeper from Mysuru district, diagnosed with recurrent, inoperable hypopharyngeal cancer involving the oesophagus, has a different but equally difficult challenge. After three cycles of chemotherapy, the disease has shown partial response. Immunotherapy could offer another treatment option, but its cost remains prohibitive. Spending another ₹2.4 lakh to ₹8 lakh over the next 2 to 3 months for bi-weekly immunotherapy is virtually impossible on a ₹45,000/month income.
Science, Space & Environment Report: Cancer care: Long battle for affordable treatment. This milestone highlights indigenous research, technological self-reliance, and environmental sustainability.

articles.title: Deepavali with pets: Why pet parents are choosing quieter holiday getaways
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: As fireworks unsettle dogs and cats, pet owners are trading noisy city celebrations for countryside retreats, pet hostels and quieter holidays

As Deepavali approaches, pets often become anxious at the sound of firecrackers. Dogs and cats may hide under beds or in dark corners, while some lose interest in playtime, walks and even pee breaks. For pet owners, finding ways to ease their distress is an ongoing challenge. Some who love celebrating Deepavali but cannot bear to see their pets shivering and panting are now choosing quieter destinations to spend the festival.
Frodo from Bengaluru | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement

Pet parent JP Daisy boards her cat at a hostel in Hyderabad’s Kokapet with soundproof rooms during Deepavali. Watching her usually docile Siamese, Sharpay, run helter-skelter as firecracker noise peaks in the evening makes Daisy anxious. “She is a lightweight cat and usually eats very little. During Deepavali, she stops eating. One of our friends suggested a place to board her. Sharpay is not clingy, so boarding her is easy,” she says.

Pet boarding facilities also see a surge in demand during festivals, and not just from people travelling. With diyas lit in homes, unattended flames can pose a safety risk. At Pet Cafe Hyderabad, a boarding facility and restaurant in Banjara Hills, founder Deven Baheti says regulars book slots weeks, sometimes months, ahead of Deepavali.

“The open space and location make it comfortable for pets. Ours is a quiet locality, with few homes bursting firecrackers. To further drown out the noise, we play calming music, use vet-approved anti-anxiety drops and essential oils, and apply calming sprays to help them relax,” says Deven.

With boarding (charges of ₹1000 per day) slots fully booked, Deven and his team are preparing to keep the pets occupied with play and grooming sessions. “We do it for the love of animals. Even reactive pets are managed by a few of us and kept in separate enclosures, away from the friendly ones.”

Voicing use of vet-approved calming drops Bengaluru based Neeta Sharma said “That is the only way to calm our pet rescued Indie Frodo. The other two a labrador and a Beagle don’t care much about the sound.”
A boarder at Pet Cafe Hyd | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement

Not all pet parents can board their pets, or are comfortable with the idea. Many instead look for pet-friendly homestays and resorts away from the city. With several properties now welcoming pets, finding the right one is the only challenge. In Chevella, about 50 kilometres from Hyderabad, homestays have become a welcome respite for pet owners. Ramya R, a pet parent, says the search for a suitable getaway begins soon after Ganesh Chaturthi. “The crackers on visarjan days are a reminder that we need to start looking.”

Pollam Gattu, a farmhouse in Chevella surrounded by carrot and flower fields, has become their regular Deepavali escape. The area sees fewer firecrackers than the city, making it a quieter retreat. “In villages, it is relatively quieter than in the city. I can’t say it is absolutely silent, but it is not as noisy with firecrackers as the city is,” she says.

articles.title: Google sued over suicide-related AI chats on school computer
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The teenager was not able to access Google's Gemini app, nor OpenAI's ChatGPT, because they were blocked by her school
The parents of a 13-year-old girl have sued Google claiming she planned a potential suicide and funeral using its AI technology on a school-issued computer.

Filed Monday in a California court, the complaint is the first known case accusing Google of negligence related to AI integrations on Chromebooks, the tech giant's low-cost laptops used by millions of students in the United States and around the world.

The teenager was not able to access Google's Gemini app, nor OpenAI's ChatGPT, because they were blocked by her school. She was nonetheless still able to use Google's search engine, which contains AI-powered tools.
Those features were notably not among the tools that Google announced this week will be disabled by default for students.

"Schools should turn search off and keep it off until Google removes AI mode from search or ensures that every single student is always safe when they're interacting with AI," Andrew Liddell, one of the family's attorneys, told AFP on Thursday.
The complaint alleges that the child had been a "happy 13-year-old girl" in North Carolina who received great grades, played music and participated in Girl Scouts.

Despite "no history" of mental illness, within months of using Google's AI-powered search on her school laptop, she began a "quiet spiral into a severe psychological crisis" according to the complaint.
On March 17, the school's monitoring software flagged a document titled "Funeral," and the school notified her parents.
Her mother then saw the child writing a farewell letter in real-time after logging into her daughter's account, and her father intervened.
"We are reviewing the claims in the lawsuit and we take this very seriously," Google spokesperson Jose Castaneda told AFP.

articles.title: Nashra Naim elected first woman vice-president of AMU students’ union in 105-year history
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Women candidates won six of the 13 posts, a record five of the 10 cabinet member posts, in the first elections after an eight-year gap

Women candidates created history in the Aligarh Muslim University (AMU) Students’ Union (AMUSU) elections, winning six of the 13 posts, including vice-president, the results of which were announced on Friday (November 6, 2026).

Nashra Naim became the first woman to be elected vice-president of the students’ union in the 105-year history of the institution. She secured 7,091 votes, defeating her nearest rival, who polled 5,818 votes, according to the result details.
Women candidates also won a record five of the 10 cabinet member posts, marking a significant increase in their representation in the students’ union.
The post of president was won by Mohammad Noman Ashraf, who secured victory by a margin of more than 4,100 votes, while Mohammad Hamdan was elected secretary, the results showed.

The results were declared by Prof. Javaid Talib, Chief Election Officer for the AMUSU and AMU Court elections, and Prof. Nazia Hasan, Chief Election Officer for the Women’s College Students’ Union elections.
This year’s elections were significant, as they were held after an unprecedented gap of eight years, following persistent protests by students over the past three years.
A senior faculty member said the ongoing Gen Z protests had also influenced the elections.

“Unlike previous years, when campus-specific issues dominated the campaign, this time the discourse also revolved around broader national issues, including those concerning Muslims,” the faculty member said, wishing not to be named.

AMU Vice-Chancellor Prof. Naima Khatoon hailed the “peaceful conduct of the elections,” describing it as “a triumph of the highest democratic traditions” of the institution. She also welcomed the growing participation and representation of women, highlighting the importance of women’s empowerment.
No incident of violence was reported during the election campaign, according to university officials.

articles.title: Suriya’s ‘Scene’: What’s the hype surrounding this Tamil Deepavali release?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Tamil cinema’s Deepavali spotlight falls on Suriya’s ‘Scene,’ a quirky investigative drama directed by Jithu Madhavan that is releasing this weekend in theatres

Scene is the scene this Deepavali in Tamil Nadu. Tamil star Suriya ’s upcoming film, Scene , directed by Malayalam filmmaker Jithu Madhavan, has single-handedly taken on the Ramayana storm down South, becoming one of the most anticipated releases this Deepavali weekend.
But what is the whole hype surrounding this Deepavali release all about?

The biggest expectation for the film is whether it will become a hat-trick of hits for Suriya at the box office in 2026. With Karuppu , Suriya became a saving grace for Tamil cinema during a devastatingly poor first half of the year, while Vishwanath & Sons offered a refreshing detour from the gore- and action-heavy films we have been getting from the industry's top stars. And now, with Scene , Suriya might just as well claim the throne as one of the few modern-day stars to deliver three hits in a calendar year. articles.title: TDP accuses Chevireddy of ‘rigging’ in Parishad polls
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: YSRCP alleges 'ragging' by ruling Alliance leaders at polling stations

Alleging various illegal activities by YSRCP leaders during ZPTC/MPTC elections, Chandragiri MLA Pulivarthi Nani and TUDA Chairman C. (Dollars) Divakar Reddy staged a protest near a polling station in Tiruchanur, Tirupati, on Thursday (November 5, 2026) evening.

The two TDP leaders demanded that the State Election Commission (SEC) conduct repolling across all polling stations in Tirupati Rural Mandal, where YSRCP leader Chevireddy Bhaskar Reddy has allegedly committed rigging of votes.

The MLA lashed out strongly against the irregularities, acts of violence, and instances of rigging that reportedly took place during the elections in the mandal. He condemned the deliberate disruption of the electoral process at polling stations — actions intended to incite fear and panic — stating that such behaviour makes a mockery of democracy.

Mr. Divakar Reddy warned the YSRCP leaders that rigging risks distorting the public mandate. He also urged the SEC to respond immediately, investigate the irregularities, and conduct a re-poll in the mandal.
Earlier, Mr. Nani's wife Pulivarthi Sudha Reddy also warned Mr. Bhaskar Reddy that she would follow him wherever he goes to prevent his alleged 'illegal' activities during the Parishad elections.

Meanwhile, Mr. Chevireddy accused the TDP leaders, including the family members of the MLA, of ragging the YSRCP cadre during the Parishad elections. He claimed that the YSRCP activists were not allowed to stay near the polling stations.

articles.title: Congress says people must express outrage over inflation by teaching BJP a lesson in upcoming polls
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Under the Modi Government, the common person’s life had become trapped in a dual vicious cycle of inflation and debt, Jairam Ramesh shared on X

The Congress on Friday (November 6, 2026) alleged that the common people have become trapped in a vicious cycle of inflation and debt, and said it was now the responsibility of voters in Punjab, Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Goa and Manipur to express their outrage against rising prices by decisively defeating the BJP in the upcoming Assembly elections.

Congress general secretary in-charge of communications Jairam Ramesh shared on X a media report which claimed that despite Government assistance under schemes such as the 'PM Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana', rising inflation in rural areas was placing an increasing financial burden on people.
The report cited a NABARD survey to claim that rural households were spending 53.5% of their total monthly income on food and beverages alone due to inflation.
In his post in Hindi, Mr. Ramesh said that under the Modi Government, the common person's life had become trapped in a dual vicious cycle of inflation and debt.

"The Modi Government's claims of rural prosperity are being exposed by surveys conducted by its own institution, NABARD. More than half of the expenditure of rural households is going towards food. Savings are shrinking, the number of people taking on debt is rising, and for informal loans, people are forced to pay annual interest rates as high as 18.3%," Mr. Ramesh said.
The Government, however, refuses to acknowledge the ground reality, leaving no room for improvement, he said.

"Persistent inflation is breaking the back of the poor and the middle class. The public is already reeling under the burden of rising prices of daily essentials, including vegetables, fruits, pulses, cooking oil, milk and flour," Mr. Ramesh claimed, adding that medical expenses were projected to rise by 10% by 2027.
Prices of items such as soap, biscuits, noodles and other daily necessities were also set to increase after Deepavali, he further claimed.
There was no relief in earnings, no check on inflation and no respite in healthcare costs, Mr. Ramesh said.
The truth about the Modi Government's "development" was that the common person's plate was shrinking, pockets were emptying and the burden of debt was growing heavier, he said.

articles.title: T.N. govt. disbands High-Level Committee on Union-State Relations
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Its mandate has been transferred to the State Law Commission, according to a Government Order issued on November 6, 2026

The High-Level Committee on Union–State Relations, constituted during the erstwhile DMK regime in Tamil Nadu, has been disbanded, and its mandate transferred to the State Law Commission, according to a Government Order (G.O.) issued on November 6, 2026.

In April 2025, then Chief Minister M.K. Stalin had announced in the Legislative Assembly the formation of a three-member high-level panel to review constitutional provisions, statutes, and policies concerning Centre–State relations, and to recommend measures to strengthen federalism and state autonomy.

The committee was chaired by retired Supreme Court Judge Justice Kurian Joseph, with retired IAS officer K. Ashok Vardhan Shetty and former State Planning Commission Vice-Chairman M. Naganathan serving as members. The committee submitted a highly acclaimed Part I of its report to then Chief Minister M.K. Stalin on February 16.
However, the TVK-led government has now chosen to dissolve the committee.

“The Tamil Nadu State Law Commission was re-constituted on 07.08.2026 and is entrusted among others with the broad mandate to examine and make recommendations on matters relating to Inter-State and Centre-State relations along with other subjects, review of the existing laws and improving the legal and institutional frame work of the State,” the G.O pointed out.

The G.O. said, “The High-Level Committee on Union-State Relations is a ‘non-statutory body’, examining various issues relating to Union-State relations, has a considerable similarity and overlap in the nature and scope of the functions entrusted to the Tamil Nadu State Law Commission. Therefore, after careful consideration, the Government have decided to discontinue the services of the High-Level Committee with immediate effect.”

While the G.O. stresses that the Committee was a “not-statutory body”, the State Law Commission, which will now take up the task, is also not a statutory body. It is an executive body created by a Government Order.

articles.title: Court acquits DMK leader Ponmudy in ‘derogatory’ religious remarks case after complainant withdraws petition
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: A BJP councillor filed a complaint alleging that Ponmudy’s speech promoted hatred and ill-will towards the Hindu religion.

A Metropolitan Magistrate court has acquitted former Tamil Nadu Minister and DMK leader K. Ponmudy of charges related to alleged derogatory remarks concerning Shaivism and Vaishnavism, following the complainant’s withdrawal of her private petition after Ponmudy issued a public apology.

The III Metropolitan Magistrate, George Town, C. Sundarapandian, pronounced the judgment on September 23, holding that the prosecution had failed to prove the charges against Mr. Ponmudy beyond reasonable doubt.

The case arose from a speech Mr. Ponmudy gave on April 6, 2025, at Anbagam, the DMK Youth Wing headquarters on Anna Salai, Teynampet, during a centenary celebration of party member Thiruvarur Thangaraj.

At the event, Mr. Ponmudy allegedly compared the religious symbols worn by Shaivites and Vaishnavites to sexual positions while narrating an anecdote involving a sex worker. The speech was uploaded on the YouTube channel Neerthirai and circulated on social media platforms.
Following public outrage, the DMK stripped Mr. Ponmudy of his party post as deputy general secretary. He later resigned as Minister.

Uma Anandan, a BJP councillor, filed a complaint alleging the remarks deliberately insulted Hindu beliefs and hurt religious sentiments. She alleged Mr. Ponmudy’s speech promoted hatred and ill-will towards the Hindu religion.

Since the Nungambakkam Police did not take any action, she filed a private complaint before the XVIII Metropolitan Magistrate Court, Saidapet, on June 12, 2025. The complaint was subsequently transferred to the special court designated to try cases involving elected MPs and MLAs, and later to the III Metropolitan Magistrate Court, George Town, following changes in the court’s jurisdiction.

During the proceedings, Mr. Ponmudy pleaded not guilty and sought trial. His counsel argued that the ingredients required to establish the offences were not made out. There were no two identifiable groups between whom enmity had been promoted to attract Section 196(1)(a), and the allegations did not satisfy the requirements of Sections 299 and 302, the defence submitted. It also contended that prior sanction under Section 217 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) had not been obtained.
However, during her examination, Ms. Anandan submitted a petition seeking withdrawal of the complaint along with an affidavit.
In her statement, Ms. Anandan said she decided to withdraw the case after he publicly apologised for his remarks and assured that he would not make such statements in the future.

articles.title: Protest suspended, not withdrawn, say KRRS leaders
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Sugarcane farmers in Belagavi claimed to have only suspended their agitation and not withdrawn it completely.
“Our protest will continue till the farmers take home a total of ₹5,500 per tonne,’’ Chunappa Pujeri, Karnataka Rajya Raitha Sangha and Hasiru Sene president, told reporters in Gurlapur on Friday.

“We have accepted the price of ₹3,600 per tonne offered by factories as a temporary solution to our problems. This is conditional to the fact that the factories have agreed to share their profits with us. This is the first time in the country that the factories have agreed to a profit-sharing formula,” Mr. Pujeri said.

“However, our demand for ₹5,500 per tonne remains unchanged. We also expect Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar to release an incentive of ₹1,000 per tonne as State Advised Price. The State government in neighbouring Maharashtra has promised to release ₹3,900 in the first instalment, ₹100 later and ₹200 if the Union government revises the Minimum Selling Price (MSP) of sugar. The Tamil Nadu government is releasing an SAP of ₹700 per tonne, in addition to the centrally mandated Fair and Remunerative Price. The governments in UP and Haryana are also offering incentives. Karnataka should do so to,” he said.

Meanwhile, farmers in Vijayapura demanded that the profit-sharing formula agreed upon in Belagavi be implemented across the State. KRRS leaders submitted a memorandum to the Deputy Commissioner K. Anand. He responded by saying that he would convene a meeting of all factories and farmers’ leaders in Vijayapura on Saturday.

“There are 10 sugar factories in the district, but all of them are not paying the same price. Last year, while the factories in the Krishna river belt paid around ₹3,300 per tonne, those in the Bhima river belt paid only around ₹3,000. This year, we want all the factories to pay ₹3,600 per tonne,” said Shantagouda Patil, KRRS leader. Sangamesh Sagar, Ramanagouda Patil, Dayananda Koli, Mahadeva Banasode, Sangappa Takke, Abhishekha Hoogar, Mudakanna and other leaders were present.

In Bagalkot, however, farmers leaders refused to accept the price of ₹3,600 offered by factories. “We have seen before our own eyes that a politician who was a director in one cooperative factory has now set up 20 private factories. It shows that they are regularly making profits. If they want to make unlimited money, why should the farmers suffer? We want ₹5,500 per tonne for sugarcane,” they alleged.

Meanwhile, Raju Shetti, former MP and founder of the Swabhimani Shetkari Sanghatan (SSS), ended his national highway rasta roko protest on Friday. He announced that the State government had announced that the farmers were likely to get ₹4,200 in three installments. The factories will first pay ₹3,900 per tonne before crushing, ₹100 after the end of crushing and ₹200 per tonne if the Union government revises MSP for sugar. This was announced after a meeting of factories and farmers convened by Minister Hassan Mushrif, Mr. Shetti said.
He gave the credit to the united struggle of Karnataka and Maharashtra for what he called was an interim success of the agitation.
The SSS members had blocked the Pune-Bangalore highway at Kini zakat naka for two days. It was opened by Friday evening.

articles.title: $2.5 trillion wiped off Nasdaq 100 as U.S. midterm outcome adds to AI stock slump
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: Democrats’ victories raise prospect of tighter scrutiny of data-centre projects as investors reassess AI spending; Indian equities buck global market weakness

Global technology stocks tumbled on fears that the massive infrastructure investments underpinning the artificial intelligence (AI) boom may take longer to build, finance and monetise, even as Indian equities bucked the worldwide sell-off with a sharp rally on November 6.

The sell-off, fuelled by concerns over mounting AI-related capital expenditure and uncertain returns, gathered momentum following the U.S. midterm election results. Democrats’ victories have heightened the prospect of tighter scrutiny of data-centre projects and possible restrictions on new developments, adding to investor anxiety.

The Nasdaq-100 plunged 6.36% on November 5, erasing approximately $2.53 trillion from its aggregate adjusted market value, according to Nasdaq index data. The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.52%, while the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 4.36% and 3.44%, respectively.
Semiconductor stocks bore the brunt, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index slumping 12.2%. Nvidia lost about 9%, while AMD and Micron Technology shed more than 17% each.
The weakness spilled over into Asian markets on Friday. South Korea’s KOSPI fell 6.02%, after plunging more than 8% intraday. Japan’s Nikkei 225 declined 5.96%, while Taiwan’s TAIEX lost 4.51%.
Indian equities, however, bucked the trend. The Sensex surged 1,718 points, or 2.17%, to close at 81,028.02, while the Nifty 50 advanced 2.01% to 25,030.35.

Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) were net buyers of Indian equities worth ₹14,974.68 crore on November 5, against net sales of ₹10,444.54 crore by domestic institutional investors (DIIs), provisional exchange data across the NSE, BSE and MSEI showed.

A Macquarie Research note flagged potential regulatory headwinds for data-centre development following election outcomes in Texas, Georgia and Ohio, where proposals to impose moratoriums or restrictions on new projects could affect the industry.

Greater scrutiny of power connections, backup-generator emissions, water consumption, zoning and taxation could prolong approvals and raise project costs. The impact may be more pronounced for projects in the pipeline than for facilities that have already secured approvals and power capacity.

Macquarie said approved but unleased data-centre capacity could gain value if fresh supply faces delays, benefiting well-capitalised operators with access to power and approved sites. It remained positive on the digital infrastructure sector.

articles.title: Bangladesh rescues Rohingya refugees in border gun battle
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: One soldier was killed in the clash on November 5 night, the military's Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said.

Bangladesh security forces rescued at least 57 people, including Rohingya refugees, during a gun battle with suspected human traffickers near the Myanmar border, the military said on Friday (November 6, 2026).
One soldier was killed in the clash on Thursday (November 5, 2026) night, the military's Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said.

ISPR said that security forces launched an operation in the hills of Rongikhali in Teknaf, close to the border with Myanmar, after receiving a tip-off that an armed gang of 15 to 16 suspected traffickers had abducted around 120 Rohingya refugees and Bangladeshis.
"During the exchange of fire, an army soldier, Md. Titash Sheikh, was shot. The bullet struck his left shoulder. He was bleeding profusely," the statement said.
Bangladesh hosts more than 1.2 million Rohingya refugees, most of whom fled a brutal military crackdown in neighbouring Myanmar in 2017.
Many live in sprawling camps around Cox's Bazar, near the border, where trafficking gangs prey on refugees seeking work or passage abroad.
The 2017 Myanmar crackdown, which saw Rohingya villages burned and civilians killed, is the subject of a genocide case at the UN's top court in The Hague.

Many live in sprawling camps around Cox's Bazar, near the border, where trafficking gangs prey on refugees seeking work or passage abroad.

articles.title: Iran Guards say two tankers caught fire in Hormuz
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Since the outbreak of the West Asia war on February 28, Tehran has sought to limit traffic through the strategic waterway, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil consumption

Iran's Revolutionary Guards said in a statement carried by state media on Friday (November 6, 2026) that two oil tankers caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz, a day after Tehran claimed five other tankers had similar fates.
Since the outbreak of the West Asia war on February 28, Tehran has sought to limit traffic through the strategic waterway, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil consumption.
The United States has in response imposed a blockade on Iranian ports and escorted tankers through the strait.

U.S. Central Command said last month that it had helped Gulf countries export 1.5 billion barrels of oil via Hormuz since the summer and has recently said that all mines have been cleared from the waterway.

"Two violating oil tankers — one east of the Strait of Hormuz and the other within the Strait itself — that attempted to transit via an unauthorised route struck mines," the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, the ideological arm of Iran's military, said in a statement carried by state TV.

"The two tankers had deactivated all of their navigation and identification systems and were attempting to exit the Strait of Hormuz... with the support of the aggressor and terrorist American military, but following the collision with mines, they caught fire and were brought to a stop," the statement added.
On Thursday (November 5, 2026), Iranian media reported that five oil tankers and a tugboat caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz in similar incidents.
There has, however, been no confirmation of any of these incidents from maritime officials.

articles.title: Trump discusses West Asia de-escalation with Qatar's Emir
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The telephone call between Trump and Qatar's Emir Sheik Tamim bin Hamad al Thani centred on international efforts to end tensions, according to a statement from the Qatari ruler's media office

U.S. President Donald Trump has discussed efforts to de-escalate tensions in the West Asia in a telephone call with Qatar's Emir as the region remained on edge over the possibility of renewed U.S. military action against Iran.
The telephone call between Mr. Trump and Qatar's Emir Sheik Tamim bin Hamad al Thani centred on international efforts to end tensions, according to a statement from the Qatari ruler's media office.
The two discussed in particular Qatar's mediation efforts aimed at reaching “a comprehensive agreement that ends the crisis and achieves security and stability in the region.”

Qatar has been mediating between the United States and Iran to end the war. Qatar and other U.S.-allied Gulf Arab countries came under heavy fire from Iran earlier in the U.S.-Iran war and have been anxious to avoid a new escalation that could leave them vulnerable to attacks.

During the call, Sheik Tamim “stressed the importance of continuing dialogue and adopting diplomatic means to resolve disputes, sparing the region further escalation, and ensuring freedom of maritime navigation and the security of energy supplies,” according to the statement.

fullParagraphs: Technology shares sold ‌off ⁠dramatically on November 5 ⁠on growing concerns that a new Congress will slow AI development, and ​also on fears ‌that the massive capital expense of building out AI will not yield sufficient ‌returns

Technology shares sold ‌off ⁠dramatically on Thursday (November 5, 2026) ⁠on growing concerns that a new Congress will slow AI development, and ​also on fears ‌that the massive capital expense of building out AI will not yield sufficient ‌returns. The White House ⁠did not immediately respond to a request ‌for comment about why the meeting was postponed.

articles.title: Keralam’s mangrove cover expanded in past decade despite prior decline, finds study
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Study by ICAR-Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute based in Kochi compared satellite images from 2017 and 2026 to map changes in mangrove vegetation across Keralam’s coastal districts
Mangrove cover in Keralam registered an overall increase over the past decade, a new study by ICAR-Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute (CMFRI) has found.

The study, presented at the international symposium on fisheries and remote sensing hosted at CMFRI, compared satellite images from 2017 and 2026 to map changes in mangrove vegetation across Keralam’s coastal districts. It found an overall rise in mangrove cover during the period, despite the State having lost nearly 90% of its mangroves over the past five decades, a statement issued by CMFRI in Kochi said.

Mangroves serve as vital breeding and nursery grounds for fish, protect coastlines from cyclones and storm surges, and help absorb atmospheric carbon. The findings highlight the potential of satellite-based monitoring to track mangrove recovery and support conservation efforts along Keralam’s coast.

The three-day international symposium is being jointly organised by Trevor Platt Science Foundation, Department of Chemical Oceanography of the Cochin University of Science and Technology (CUSAT), CMFRI and Marine Biological Association of India.

Another study presented at the symposium highlighted the increasing incidence of marine heatwaves in the Bay of Bengal. The region experienced more than 100 marine heatwave events between 1982 and 2023, with both their frequency and cumulative intensity showing an increasing trend.
The study was presented by the Department of Oceanography of Shahjalal University of Science and Technology, Bangladesh.

articles.title: Air quality of Delhi worsens, many parts reel under ‘severe’ level air pollution
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Many parts of the national capital, including IIT Delhi, ITO, Dwarka, Rohini, Punjabi Bagh, Alipur, Bawana, and Jahangirpuri, witnessed “severe” level air pollution

The overall air quality of Delhi worsened and continued to be in the “very poor” category on Friday (November 6, 2026) morning, while many parts of the city reeled under “severe” level of air pollution, according to official data.
Many parts of the national capital, including IIT Delhi, ITO, Dwarka, Rohini, Punjabi Bagh, Alipur, Bawana, and Jahangirpuri, witnessed “severe” level air pollution.
Other cities and towns in north India, including Noida, Gurugram, and Faridabad also witnessed overall “very poor” air quality, on Friday (November 6, 2026) morning.
The 24-hour average Air Quality Index (AQI) of Delhi was 391 (very poor) at 9 a.m. on Friday, as per Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) data.
“Severe” level air pollution affects healthy people and seriously impacts those with existing diseases, as per the CPCB.
The overall air quality of Delhi is likely to be in the “severe” category for three days, as per the Central government’s ‘Air Quality Early Warning System for Delhi’.

The 24-hour average overall Air Quality Index (AQI) of Delhi stood at 369 (very poor) on Thursday at 4 p.m. on Thursday, slightly down from 377 (very poor) a day earlier, as per the Central Pollution Control Board’s daily bulletin, which is treated as the day’s AQI. A higher AQI means worsening of air quality.

Every winter, air pollution spikes in Delhi-NCR and many parts of the larger Indo-Gangetic Plains, mainly due to meteorological factors such as lower wind speeds and a drop in temperature. Also, pollution from stubble burning during October and November and bursting of firecrackers during the festive season add to existing pollution from vehicles and dust, worsening the air quality.

Many parts of the national capital, including IIT Delhi, ITO, Dwarka, Rohini, Punjabi Bagh, Alipur, Bawana, and Jahangirpuri, witnessed “severe” level air pollution

The overall air quality of Delhi worsened and continued to be in the “very poor” category on Friday (November 6, 2026) morning, while many parts of the city reeled under “severe” level of air pollution, according to official data.

Many parts of the national capital, including IIT Delhi, ITO, Dwarka, Rohini, Punjabi Bagh, Alipur, Bawana, and Jahangirpuri, witnessed “severe” level air pollution.

Other cities and towns in north India, including Noida, Gurugram, and Faridabad also witnessed overall “very poor” air quality, on Friday (November 6, 2026) morning.

The 24-hour average Air Quality Index (AQI) of Delhi was 391 (very poor) at 9 a.m. on Friday, as per Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) data.

“Severe” level air pollution affects healthy people and seriously impacts those with existing diseases, as per the CPCB.

The overall air quality of Delhi is likely to be in the “severe” category for three days, as per the Central government’s ‘Air Quality Early Warning System for Delhi’.

The 24-hour average overall Air Quality Index (AQI) of Delhi stood at 369 (very poor) on Thursday at 4 p.m. on Thursday, slightly down from 377 (very poor) a day earlier, as per the Central Pollution Control Board’s daily bulletin, which is treated as the day’s AQI. A higher AQI means worsening of air quality.

Every winter, air pollution spikes in Delhi-NCR and many parts of the larger Indo-Gangetic Plains, mainly due to meteorological factors such as lower wind speeds and a drop in temperature. articles.title: ACB detects 90 suspicious UPI transactions at LB Nagar fire station
