fullParagraphs: Around 90 suspicious UPI transactions, ranging from ₹1,000 to ₹4,500 each, were detected on the mobile phones of staff at the LB Nagar Fire Station during a surprise check by the Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) on Friday, November 6.

The transactions had taken place during the preceding week amid allegations that fire station personnel were collecting amounts higher than the prescribed fee for issuing temporary firecracker shop licences. The prescribed online fee for a temporary licence is ₹500. The ACB found that nearly 397 applications had been received for such licences, of which 26 were still pending.

The bureau is probing the reasons for the delay in processing the applications and examining the alleged collection of excess amounts. The ACB has appealed to the public to report any demand for money beyond the prescribed fee or unexplained delays in processing applications. Complaints can be made through its toll-free number 1064 or WhatsApp number 9440446106.

Political & National Report: ACB detects 90 suspicious UPI transactions at LB Nagar fire station. This development is a key milestone in India's ongoing legislative, judicial, and constitutional governance framework.

fullParagraphs: Cyberabad Police have initiated steps to explore a one-way traffic system along the Biodiversity Junction, Mindspace and HITEC City corridor to ease congestion during peak hours.

Cyberabad Commissioner of Police M. Ramesh, accompanied by Joint Commissioner of Police (Traffic) Sunpreet Singh, RTC officials and other traffic police personnel, inspected the proposed route on Friday. The inspection covered Biodiversity Junction, IKEA, T-Works, Qualcomm, Dallas Centre Road and surrounding areas.

The proposed one-way corridor would cover Biodiversity Junction, Mindspace Rotary, Times Square Road, Knowledge City Road, Qualcomm and Dallas Centre Road. Officials examined traffic flow patterns, road conditions and major conflict points along the stretch to assess the feasibility of the proposal and identify measures to reduce congestion.

During the inspection, Mr Ramesh instructed officials to prepare a detailed report covering a comprehensive traffic flow study, identified bottlenecks and conflict points, supported by relevant visuals.

He also directed them to conduct a block-wise assessment of buildings contributing to traffic congestion, including the anticipated traffic impact, vehicle volume generated by each building, availability of parking facilities and parking capacity.
The exercise aims to identify suitable traffic management measures and streamline vehicular movement around T-Hub, IKEA, Knowledge City, Qualcomm and Biodiversity.

articles.title: Greater flamingos sighted for the first time at Kere Bhosga
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The four-day Karnataka Rajyotsava Bird Count (KRBC), an initiative by eBird held from October 30 to November 2, recorded 139 bird species, generating 79 checklists with 18 birds participating, highlighting the region’s avian diversity. A major highlight was the sighting of greater flamingos at Bhosga Kere for the first time.

A bird walk on this occasion was organised by local group Winged Endeavours as part of the first State-wide initiative under the eBird platform; the exercise aimed to document Karnataka’s bird diversity, recording 62 species across the city during the birding session.
Painted storks sighted at the S.B. lake during the bird count event in Kalaburagi. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT

K.S. Aishwarya of Winged Endeavours led the participants of the bird walk across different locations, including lakes and birding hot spots in the city, introducing them to birdwatching and encouraging them to document local birdlife.
Among the species recorded were the purple heron, river tern and Eurasian spoonbill. Migratory visitors included the greater flamingo, common sandpiper, northern shoveler and rosy starling.

Explaining bird migration patterns, Ms. Aishwarya said the movement was driven primarily by a lack of food availability. Depletion of food resources in their native habitats prompted birds to move to regions offering better feeding opportunities. Some destinations also served as breeding grounds, improving the survival prospects of their young, she said.

Kalaburagi’s relatively mild winters make it a suitable seasonal habitat for migratory birds escaping severe cold in their native ranges. Winter visitors are generally spotted in the region from October to early March, she added.

The northern shoveler migrates from Russia, Siberia, Europe and Central Asia, while the common sandpiper arrives from Europe and northern Asia. Greater flamingos visit from parts of Central Asia, including Kazakhstan, and the Middle East. Rosy starlings arrive from Eastern Europe and Central Asia, attracted by grain crops and insects.

Systematic documentation helps understand their seasonal movements and distribution, they said. The observations uploaded to eBird provide useful data for researchers and conservationists studying bird diversity and migration patterns.

articles.title: Delhi’s Mustafabad election official lodges police complaint seeking FIR over false Form 7s after The Hindu report
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Delhi’s north east District Election Officer (DEO) Ajay Kumar told The Hindu that they have verified the news report independently and found 36 of the 37 Form 7s to be false/fabricated

The Electoral Registration Officer (ERO) of Mustafabad constituency has lodged a police complaint on Friday (November 7, 2026) seeking FIR under Section 31 of RP Act against the BLA following The Hindu report that false Form 7s have been filed seeking deletions of voters who are living at their addresses.

The north east District Election Officer (DEO ) Ajay Kumar told The Hindu that they have verified the news report independently and found 36 of the 37 Form 7s to be false/fabricated. “In connection with reports appearing in print and social media regarding false and fabricated Form-7, a police complaint has been lodged today by the ERO for registration of an FIR under Section 31 of the RP 1950 against the BLA,” a press release from his office also stated.

The Hindu reported on October 30 that in polling part area 129 of Mustafabad constituency, 28 Form 7s seeking deletions of electors found to be living in the area were filed by a BLA registered under Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), Chandra Shekhar Nainwal, as per Election Commission of India (ECI) records till October 28. While Mr. Nainwal denied filing these applications and any association with BJP, speaking to The Hindu , nine fresh applications were filed naming him as objector on October 29-30. The reasons cited in these applications were “absent/permanently shifted” and “dead”.

It further said that all 37 forms were scrutinised by the BLO/AERO who found that three electors who were claimed to be dead were found alive at their addresses. All others were also found living at their addresses, as reported by The Hindu .

“Only one case is found to be true whereas 36 cases are found to be false/fabricated. Since the BLA/Objector has knowingly made false statement or declaration in the Form-7, action under Section 31 of the RP act has been invoked for making false statement /declaration in writing in connection with preparation /revision of electoral roll,” the release mentioned.

It stated that verification and inquiry in respect of other Form-7 applications is in progress. As per The Hindu analysis, over 77% of the total 1,021 Form 7s received till November 3 names 20 BJP BLAs as objector. All are against Muslim electors, and several have been found residing at their addresses in different areas.
“Necessary action, as per the guidelines of the Election Commission of India and the extant Act, shall be taken,” the DEO stated in the press release.
Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls / Election Commission of India

📰 Delhi’s Mustafabad election official lodges police complaint seeking FIR over false Form 7s after The Hindu report

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

Delhi’s north east District Election Officer (DEO) Ajay Kumar told The Hindu that they have verified the news report independently and found 36 of the 37 Form 7s to be false/fabricated

The Electoral Registration Officer (ERO) of Mustafabad constituency has lodged a police complaint on Friday (November 7, 2026) seeking FIR under Section 31 of RP Act against the BLA following The Hindu report that false Form 7s have been filed seeking deletions of voters who are living at their addresses.

The north east District Election Officer (DEO ) Ajay Kumar told The Hindu that they have verified the news report independently and found 36 of the 37 Form 7s to be false/fabricated. “In connection with reports appearing in print and social media regarding false and fabricated Form-7, a police complaint has been lodged today by the ERO for registration of an FIR under Section 31 of the RP 1950 against the BLA,” a press release from his office also stated.

The Hindu reported on October 30 that in polling part area 129 of Mustafabad constituency, 28 Form 7s seeking deletions of electors found to be living in the area were filed by a BLA registered under Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), Chandra Shekhar Nainwal, as per Election Commission of India (ECI) records till October 28. While Mr. Nainwal denied filing these applications and any association with BJP, speaking to The Hindu , nine fresh applications were filed naming him as objector on October 29-30. The reasons cited in these applications were “absent/permanently shifted” and “dead”.

It further said that all 37 forms were scrutinised by the BLO/AERO who found that three electors who were claimed to be dead were found alive at their addresses. All others were also found living at their addresses, as reported by The Hindu .

“Only one case is found to be true whereas 36 cases are found to be false/fabricated. Since the BLA/Objector has knowingly made false statement or declaration in the Form-7, action under Section 31 of the RP act has been invoked for making false statement /declaration in writing in connection with preparation /revision of electoral roll,” the release mentioned.

It stated that verification and inquiry in respect of other Form-7 applications is in progress. As per The Hindu analysis, over 77% of the total 1,021 Form 7s received till November 3 names 20 BJP BLAs as objector. All are against Muslim electors, and several have been found residing at their addresses in different areas.

“Necessary action, as per the guidelines of the Election Commission of India and the extant Act, shall be taken,” the DEO stated in the press release.

articles.title: Rajasthan police rescue six minors forced into sex work, five arrested
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The police acted after taking cognisance of a ‘Ground Zero’ report in August by The Hindu.

The Rajasthan police has rescued six minor girls of the Banchhada community in Jhalawar district and arrested five people – most of whom were related to the girls – for allegedly pushing them into sex work, officers said on Friday (November 6, 2026).

Speaking to The Hindu , Jhalawar Superintendent of Police (SP) Amit Kumar said that the girls, aged between 12 and 17, were rescued in raids conducted in the Bhawanimandi area on November 3 and that medical and forensic examinations have confirmed sexual exploitation of five of the girls.
Two of the girls have also tested positive for sexually transmitted diseases (STDs).

Mr. Kumar said that the action was taken after the police took cognisance of a ‘Ground Zero’ report by The Hindu , which had in August highlighted the problem of children being forced into the sex trade in Madhya Pradesh’s Mandsaur, Neemuch and Ratlam districts.

The Banchhada community, a de-notified tribe , is mainly spread across various districts of Madhya Pradesh’s Nimar region and Rajasthan’s Mewar region. The community has long been infamous for being involved in traditional sex work, often by forcing their daughters into sex work from an early age, with their family members and relatives working as pimps.
As per the Jhalawar police, the community has a significant population in about 5-6 villages in the district.

Mr. Kumar said that an SIT headed by Additional SP Ayush Shrotriya was formed for the operation, after which two officers were sent to localities where the community had a presence to gather digital evidence with the help of spy cameras.

“After verifying the digital evidence and intelligence inputs, raids were conducted in localities of the community with over 100 personnel – including women personnel in civil dress – and six girls were rescued,” the officer said.

Mr. Kumar said that an FIR under Sections 3, 4, and 5 of the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, and Sections 5, 6, 11, 12 and 17 of the The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act has been lodged at Bhawanimandi police station.
He said that a separate SIT under Additional SP Bhagchandra Meena has been formed for further investigation into the case.

articles.title: Yadgir bandh evokes good response
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Yadgir bandh called by various organisations under the leadership of former Minister Narasimha Naik (Rajugouda) evoked a good response across the Yadgir district headquarters, as well as in Shorapur and Hunsagi taluks, on Friday.

​The agitation was staged to demand the uninterrupted release of water from the Basavasagar reservoir through the Narayanpur Left and Right Bank Canals until the end of November to protect standing crops, including paddy, green chili, and cotton.
​Commercial establishments, markets, and shops voluntarily shut down operations until 3 p.m. in solidarity with the farmers. However, public transport remained largely unaffected.
​Hundreds of farmers gathered near the Tahsildar’s office in Yadgir before marching to the Subhash Chandra Bose Circle, where they staged a demonstration for several hours.

​Addressing the rally, Mr. Naik alleged that despite sufficient water storage in the reservoir, discharges were being routed overnight to neighboring Telangana while local agricultural requirements were overlooked. Rebutting district in-charge Minister Sharan Prakash Patil’s denial of the allegations, Mr. Naik claimed that local farmers possessed video evidence documenting the inter-State water transfer.

​He appealed to Large and Medium Industries Minister M.B. Patil to allocate at least 14 tmcft of water to Yadgir district to save standing crops, highlighting that 28 tmcft of water had already been reserved for drinking purposes in Vijayapura and Bagalkot districts.

​Mr. Naik also urged Superintendent of Police Pruthvik Shankar to withdraw cases registered against farmers during previous agitations, offering to have himself booked first instead. He warned that the agitation would be intensified if Krishna Bhagya Jala Nigama Limited enforces its proposed Warabandhi shutdown starting November 12.
​The protest garnered support from multiple farmer associations, pro-Kannada outfits, Dalit organisations, and the local Advocates’ Association.

​A formal memorandum addressed to the Chief Minister was submitted through Deputy Commissioner Rahul Pandve, who assured the protesters that their demands and grievances would be forwarded to higher authorities promptly.
​Basavaraj Veebhutihalli, Rachanagouda Mudnal, Mahesh Reddy Mudnal, Devendra Nath Nad, Lalita Anapur, Mareppa Chattarkar, Mareppa Naik, Bheemu Naik and others were present at the demonstration.

Yemen’s Houthis said the toll from an airstrike on a market in Taiz province, southwestern Yemen, on Friday (November 6, 2026) increased to 30 dead, as the warring sides traded blame for the attack.

“Saudi enemy aircraft targeted the Hadara market in Waziyah district, resulting in 30 deaths and eight injuries,” the Houthis’ Health Ministry said in a statement carried by the group’s Saba news agency, updating an earlier toll.
It would be one of the deadliest attacks since fighting resumed between the Houthis and Saudi-backed government forces.
A Houthi Health Ministry spokesperson, Anees Alsabahi, told Houthi-run TV Al Masirah that 15 people were also wounded in the airstrikes on the market in al-Waziyah in the province of Taiz.
He said that the death toll was expected to rise from the airstrikes, which he blamed on the Saudi-led coalition.

Local authorities in Taiz acknowledged that an attack on a busy market killed and wounded people, without providing details on the actual toll. But the authorities in Taiz blamed the Houthis for the incident. They said that no airstrikes were carried out in the area.
The Associated Press couldn't immediately independently verify the claims of responsibility.

articles.title: Epic failures: on electoral roll, welfare
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: The electoral roll cannot be used to determine welfare beneficiaries

Union Panchayati Raj Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh’s statement that voter identity cards, with biometric authentication, will replace Aadhaar as the basis for identifying beneficiaries and making payments under his Ministry’s schemes runs contrary to existing laws and regulations. Essentially, the electoral roll, prepared in several States through the flawed Special Intensive Revision (SIR) by the Election Commission of India (ECI), will become the dataset to vet the identities of beneficiaries. This contradicts the Supreme Court’s May 27 judgment on the Bihar SIR and its observations while hearing petitions against West Bengal’s orders removing people deleted during the SIR from the Public Distribution System and the Annapurna Yojana. The Court held that the ECI may undertake only a “limited enquiry” into citizenship to decide who belongs on the electoral roll, and that “any action taken pursuant thereto is confined to electoral consequences alone”. The consequence of deletion from the rolls, it said, is “correspondingly limited” to a person’s place on the roll and their right to vote. The Court also called the EPIC “a derivative document, issued on the basis of inclusion in the electoral roll”, and held that relying on it to verify that very roll would defeat the exercise. It is ironic that Mr. Singh now wants this “derivative document” to be the determinant of welfare benefits.

Not every citizen is an eligible voter, and tying benefits to the electoral roll is illogical and also cruel. In West Bengal, lakhs were deleted from the rolls , many for dubious “logical discrepancies”. In the appeals heard for reinstatement, 93% resulted in the restoration of names by September 2026, pointing to massive pre-election disenfranchisement. The Court has stated that it is yet to adjudicate on the legality of the ECI’s “logical discrepancies” method. The SIR was designed by the ECI to restrict enrolment through stringent residency criteria; thus, itinerant voters had to prove their eligibility. The Opposition, civil society and even some of the BJP’s allies have objected to this, but the BJP refuses to acknowledge the SIR’s flaws. This is partly because it has benefited from disenfranchisement — as in West Bengal. But the Minister’s remarks suggest another reason. The BJP-led coalition sees the pruned electoral rolls as a way to limit welfare, especially at a time when growth in tax revenues has slowed because of the Centre’s policies. Inordinately delaying the Census, changing the procedure to appoint Election Commissioners, who then run an exercise that disenfranchises millions by design, and now, using the resultant rolls to decide who gets welfare, all cut at the heart of the painstakingly built constitutional welfare state. The sooner the Court decides the petitions against the SIR, and reiterates that its rolls cannot be used to curtail welfare, the better.

In the appeals heard for reinstatement, 93% resulted in the restoration of names by September 2026, pointing to massive pre-election disenfranchisement. The Court has stated that it is yet to adjudicate on the legality of the ECI’s “logical discrepancies” method. The SIR was designed by the ECI to restrict enrolment through stringent residency criteria; thus, itinerant voters had to prove their eligibility. The Opposition, civil society and even some of the BJP’s allies have objected to this, but the BJP refuses to acknowledge the SIR’s flaws. This is partly because it has benefited from disenfranchisement — as in West Bengal. But the Minister’s remarks suggest another reason. The BJP-led coalition sees the pruned electoral rolls as a way to limit welfare, especially at a time when growth in tax revenues has slowed because of the Centre’s policies. Inordinately delaying the Census, changing the procedure to appoint Election Commissioners, who then run an exercise that disenfranchises millions by design, and now, using the resultant rolls to decide who gets welfare, all cut at the heart of the painstakingly built constitutional welfare state. The sooner the Court decides the petitions against the SIR, and reiterates that its rolls cannot be used to curtail welfare, the better.

articles.title: Israel Opposition eases on ultra-Orthodox draft to oust Netanyahu
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Listing the most important goals as removing Netanyahu and avoiding new elections, Opposition partner Avigdor Liberman said it was time to compromise and "understand that trying to have everything risks getting nothing".

Israel's Opposition saw a new path on Friday (October 6, 2026) to oust Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu as one of its leaders backtracked on demands that ultra-Orthodox Jews serve in the military, opening the door to a once improbable alliance with the community.
Neither Mr. Netanyahu nor Opposition chief Gadi Eisenkot reached a majority in the October 27 election, with Israeli society highly polarised over Mr. Netanyahu and worn down by three years of war.

Mr. Eisenkot, a former military commander whose campaign sought to appeal to secular and liberal Israelis, could form a government with Israeli-Arabs, whose seat count soared on anger over Mr. Netanyahu's far-right government.

But an alliance with Israeli-Arabs faces strong disagreement from Opposition partner Avigdor Liberman, a one-time aide to Mr. Netanyahu who now sharply criticises the Prime Minister but shares his hawkish views on the Palestinians.

Mr. Liberman said on Friday (November 6, 2026) he would not back down on refusing to work with Israeli-Arabs but called for talks with ultra-Orthodox Jews, even though he has berated the community for years and ran on promises to end its exemption from Israel's mandatory military service.

Listing the most important goals as removing Mr. Netanyahu and avoiding new elections, Mr. Liberman said it was time to compromise and "understand that trying to have everything risks getting nothing".
"This also includes the issue of the conscription law," he said in a social media statement.

"This pains me, and I know it pains many others as well. But given the full range of challenges we face today, the national interest of the State of Israel and the Jewish people must take precedence over all other considerations."

President Isaac Herzog plans on Sunday (November 8, 2026) to announce who will have the first chance to form a government — most logically Mr. Eisenkot, as he has received the most endorsements thanks to support from Israeli-Arabs.
Yair Golan, Israel's main left-wing leader and part of the Opposition bloc, said "serious work" was underway to form a coalition.

articles.title: Two USCIRF officials claim vigilante attacks on gurdwaras in India
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: India describes U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom as a biased organisation that lacks credibility

Two officials of an American advisory body on religious freedom have claimed that Sikh gurdwaras in India have been targeted with vigilante attacks and urged the U.S. government to press New Delhi to hold perpetrators of such violence accountable.

"Over the last several weeks, Sikh gurdwaras in India have been targeted with vigilante attacks, including attempts to harm religious leaders,” U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom (USCIRF) Commissioner David Anderson said in a social media post without elaborating.
ALSO WATCH Sukhbir Singh Badal injured in knife attack inside Nanded gurdwara
Mr. Anderson said the U.S. should link security assistance to the Indian government's response to violence that stops people from exercising freedom of religious belief (FoRB).

Another USCIRF Commissioner, Joe Grogan, said attacks on houses of worship in India, including churches, gurdwaras, and mosques, undermine FoRB rights enshrined in international law. “The US government should continue to press the Indian government to hold perpetrators of such violence accountable & protect places of worship,” he said.
India describes USCIRF as a biased organisation that lacks credibility.
Established by the U.S. government in 1998 after the inaction of the International Religious Freedom Act, the recommendations of USCIRF are non-binding on the U.S. State Department.

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: The electoral roll cannot be used to determine welfare beneficiaries

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Union Panchayati Raj Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh’s statement that voter identity cards, with biometric authentication, will replace Aadhaar as the basis for identifying beneficiaries and making payments under his Ministry’s schemes runs contrary to existing laws and regulations. Essentially, the electoral roll, prepared in several States through the flawed Special Intensive Revision (SIR) by the Election Commission of India (ECI), will become the dataset to vet the identities of beneficiaries. This contradicts the Supreme Court’s May 27 judgment on the Bihar SIR and its observations while hearing petitions against West Bengal’s orders removing people deleted during the SIR from the Public Distribution System and the Annapurna Yojana. The Court held that the ECI may undertake only a “limited enquiry” into citizenship to decide who belongs on the electoral roll, and that “any action taken pursuant thereto is confined to electoral consequences alone”. The consequence of deletion from the rolls, it said, is “correspondingly limited” to a person’s place on the roll and their right to vote. The Court also called the EPIC “a derivative document, issued on the basis of inclusion in the electoral roll”, and held that relying on it to verify that very roll would defeat the exercise. It is ironic that Mr. Singh now wants this “derivative document” to be the determinant of welfare benefits.

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: India must eliminate situations that lead to sewer cleaning deaths

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Despite legislation, Supreme Court orders, government programmes, the availability of mechanised cleaning technologies, and exhortations from politicians, India continues to lose sanitation workers to foreseeable, and largely preventable, circumstances. In a recent incident, four workers lost their lives in Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh , cleaning a hotel’s food-waste chamber. According to Parliament and the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis data, the number of workers who died on jobs involving sewer and septic tanks was 859 between 2014 and 2025, 498 from 2019 to mid-2026, 332 across 18 States and Union Territories in 2021-26, and 1,350 between 1993 and 2025. The figures have never tended towards zero even as the Safai Karamchari Andolan has repeatedly alleged severe under-reporting. Further, the government has maintained since at least 2021 that the practice of manually cleaning excreta from insanitary latrines has been eliminated, effectively signalling that it believes it has addressed the root of the problem when it has not, and freeing administrative bodies of the urgency of inspecting municipalities and private establishments. Members of historically marginalised castes are also overrepresented in these jobs. The law has distinguished hazardous cleaning of sewers and septic tanks from manual scavenging since 2013. Even so, persons entering them are still vulnerable to noxious gases. In Dr. Balram Singh (2023), the Court strengthened the requirements under Safai Karamchari Andolan (2014) to, among other measures, ensure outsourced sewer-cleaning contracts did not entail workers entering sewers and raise the compensation for deaths to ₹30 lakh per worker. In 2025, there was an order to end manual sewer cleaning in four metropolitan cities, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad followed a year later with notices to 15 Chief Secretaries for disobeying the 2023 order, including on the compensation.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: law / court / technology (general) / politics / civic infrastructure / parliament / employment / labour / local authority / death / Bengaluru / Hyderabad / Madhya Pradesh / Caste

He said that the unequivocal conclusion was that Israeli security forces continued to commit “war crimes, crimes against humanity, and the crime of genocide” a year after the October 2025 ceasefire agreement brokered by the U.S. The Commission’s third such submission since October 7, 2023, the report focuses on the “killings and bodily and mental harm by state actors”, predominantly Israeli security forces. It draws on medical records, satellite imagery, forensic analysis, witness testimony and videos posted by Israeli soldiers. Despite Israeli denials, the report finds that soldiers targeted Palestinian civilians, including infants, by using Artificial Intelligence (AI) to identify and execute their targets with impunity ; the report quotes top Israel officials claiming the killings. Justice Muralidhar said that more than 75,000 Palestinians including 21,500 children and 11,000 women have been killed across Palestinian territories since 2023 , and yet “little or no action” is being taken by member-states, including Israel itself. The report calls on UN members to “employ all means” to prevent the genocide, investigate and prosecute suspects for it, and establish clear rules for AI use in conflicts. The Committee had previously called on UN members to halt military transfers to Israel , and pass sanctions against those linked to child abuses, as well as to cooperate with the International Criminal Court to enforce arrest warrants against Israeli officials and soldiers.
